scope: Coverage-guided fuzzing must exercise parsers, storage log replay, userspace image metadata, sync frames, capability messages, and kernel/user ABI decoding before release.
current_evidence: Adversarial spec tests reject malformed manifests, corrupted storage logs, stale metadata, and bypass attempts.
open_gaps: Coverage-guided fuzz harnesses and corpus minimization are not wired into a repeatable release target.
graduation_criteria: Add release-running fuzz harnesses with checked seed corpora, sanitizer-compatible host builds where available, crash deduplication, and regression fixtures for every accepted crash.
cisa_alignment: Treat exploit-prone input handling as a manufacturer-owned defect class and block release when parser fuzz evidence is absent.

scope: Fault injection must cover boot artifact tamper, rollback failure, power loss, torn writes, storage driver crash/rebind, recovery repair, and sync transport disruption.
current_evidence: QEMU smoke paths include tampered artifacts, rollback-slot failure, recovery proof, storage durability, and driver restart gates.
open_gaps: Fault campaigns are focused fixtures rather than randomized or matrixed failure injection across all release profiles.
graduation_criteria: Promote storage, driver, recovery, sync, and boot fault campaigns into a release matrix with deterministic seeds, artifacts, and failure triage records.
cisa_alignment: Exercise secure-by-default behavior under failure instead of depending on customer recovery workarounds.

scope: Release artifacts must be buildable from pinned inputs with deterministic outputs or documented, bounded nondeterminism.
current_evidence: The repository pins the Zig toolchain entrypoint and keeps generated artifacts under build outputs.
open_gaps: There is no release target that performs clean rebuild comparison, records environment inputs, or proves deterministic ISO/kernel/userspace archive bytes.
graduation_criteria: Add a reproducible-build release target that performs two clean builds, compares artifact digests, records toolchain and environment metadata, and explains accepted nondeterminism.
cisa_alignment: Support supply-chain transparency and reduce unverified build inputs before customer distribution.

scope: Every release artifact must carry machine-readable SBOM data, source provenance, signer identity, measured boot inputs, and customer-verifiable digest records.
current_evidence: Userspace archives, boot measurements, signed bundle state, and launch provenance are modeled and tested.
open_gaps: Machine-readable SBOM generation, release provenance attestations, and customer-facing verification bundles are not yet emitted by the release flow.
graduation_criteria: Generate SPDX or CycloneDX SBOMs plus provenance attestations for kernels, userspace archives, tools, and ISO outputs; verify them in release tests.
cisa_alignment: Maintain SBOMs and transparent vulnerability/exploitability records for first- and third-party software.

scope: Threat-model tests must cover explicit authority, privilege boundaries, boot trust, recovery, policy mediation, storage integrity, sync trust, diagnostics privacy, and driver isolation.
current_evidence: Spec conformance and adversarial tests already encode revoked capability, expired lease, malformed manifest, corrupted log, rollback, and bypass threats.
open_gaps: The threat model is test-backed but not yet published as a reviewer-facing matrix with threat IDs, abuse cases, mitigations, and residual-risk owners.
graduation_criteria: Publish a threat-model matrix and require every P0/P1 release track to list abuse cases, mitigations, negative tests, and residual-risk decisions.
cisa_alignment: Make security properties measurable across the product lifecycle and prevent dangerous defaults from shipping silently.

scope: Unsafe Zig and kernel-adjacent sections must be inventoried, reviewed, minimized, and bound by tests before release, especially pointer casts, integer-pointer conversion, inline assembly, packed ABI structs, and user memory copies.
current_evidence: The kernel and native syscall paths centralize many low-level boundaries and have targeted negative tests around user memory and brokered devices.
open_gaps: There is no published memory-safety roadmap, unsafe-surface inventory, or required reviewer signoff for kernel and ABI pointer manipulation.
graduation_criteria: Add an unsafe-surface inventory, required audit owner, reviewer checklist, and tests for every user-memory copy, pointer conversion, inline assembly block, and kernel allocator invariant.
cisa_alignment: Treat memory-safety roadmaps and migration/mitigation evidence as mandatory for unsafe or kernel-adjacent code.

scope: Crash dumps, event-ledger exports, remote diagnostics, and support bundles must redact secrets, private object names, personal content, capability tokens, and raw memory by default.
current_evidence: Event-ledger, supervisor, and spec tests verify redacted diagnostics for crashes, permission decisions, and remote shares.
open_gaps: Raw crash dump capture policy, memory dump deny-by-default behavior, and support-bundle export review are not yet separate release gates.
graduation_criteria: Add explicit crash dump policy tests for raw memory capture denial, opt-in scoped diagnostics, capability token scrubbing, and reproducible redaction fixtures.
cisa_alignment: Keep security-sensitive telemetry safe by default and avoid shifting diagnostic privacy risk to customers.

scope: A release must have a published vulnerability disclosure policy, private intake channel, triage SLA, CVE/CWE handling process, coordinated disclosure rules, and security update commitments.
current_evidence: SECURITY.md documents the disclosure workflow and marks private intake configuration as a public-release blocker.
open_gaps: The project still needs an operational monitored private reporting channel and CNA/CVE issuance path before public release.
graduation_criteria: Configure and publish the private intake channel, define maintainers on rotation, document CVE issuance ownership, and test the end-to-end disclosure workflow before release.
cisa_alignment: Avoid the CISA bad practice of shipping without a scoped vulnerability disclosure policy and timely CVE/CWE process.

first_hardware_target.selection_reason: Single commodity x86_64 UEFI target with ACPI, integrated display output, USB xHCI input path, M.2 NVMe storage, and wired Intel I225-LM Ethernet so the first hardware proof does not depend on Wi-Fi or dongles.
first_hardware_target.boot_medium: UEFI GRUB ISO or USB image built from build/os.iso.
first_hardware_target.serial_capture: Real-machine serial, framebuffer capture, or HDMI capture logs archived under build/hardware-proofs/nuc11tnki5/ and checked by scripts/check-nuc11tnki5-hardware-proof.sh.
hardware_exit_criteria: Ten cold UEFI boots and ten warm reboots reach native-ready on the NUC11TNKi5 without panic, hang, or firmware fallback.
ACPI table discovery, APIC timer calibration, GOP framebuffer output, USB xHCI keyboard input, NVMe read/write, and Intel I225-LM transmit/receive each emit the required hardware target marker.
Twenty suspend/resume cycles preserve timer, framebuffer, USB input, NVMe, and network usability.
Ten induced crash-recovery cycles preserve the native store and produce redacted recovery diagnostics.
Every hardware proof bundle includes serial output, firmware settings, power-cycle notes, and the exact kernel/userspace artifact digests.
open_gaps: No NUC11TNKi5 serial log has been captured from real hardware yet.

UEFI handoff, ACPI parsing, APIC timer calibration, GOP framebuffer ownership, xHCI input, NVMe, Intel I225-LM, suspend/resume, and crash recovery still need real-device implementation and proof markers.

tracks.title: Object store and storage volume durability
current_evidence: Content-addressed objects use signed metadata, chunked blob records, and Merkle-addressed payload manifests.
The storage volume can save and replay segmented logs through image-backed and attached-volume paths.
Host tests cover corrupted payload rejection, malformed root-log metadata, torn-record rejection, compaction, page-sized payload reload, and shared-memory transfer into the storage service.
The first supported storage envelope is exported from storage_volume.first_supported_capacity_envelope and checked before image or attached-volume persistence.

Writes that exceed the first supported envelope have an explicit user-facing quota policy: reject without partial persistence, report storage.quota.* limit codes, and surface NoSpaceLeft at the persistence gate.
capacity_envelope: Volume image: 524288 bytes across 1024 required device sectors, with 523264 bytes available for replay logs.
Object store: 128 objects, 512 versions, 512 blobs, 192 chunks, 24 chunks per payload, 4096-byte chunks, and a 98304-byte maximum object payload.
Workspace state: 8 workspaces, 96 entries per workspace, and 16 snapshots.
Replay gate: 128 log records and 16 segment boundaries before compaction must write a new checkpoint.
Over-limit write behavior: no truncation, eviction, implicit expansion, or partial persistence; callers must free space or move to a larger product envelope before retrying.
production_gaps: Power-loss, torn-write, partial-sector corruption, migration, and long-running compaction evidence are not yet first-class gates.
The native attached-volume path needs broader QEMU evidence across cold reboot, crash before root commit, and recovery after one bad root slot.
graduation_criteria: Keep the explicit product storage limits enforced in persistence gates or replace fixed tables with bounded dynamic allocation and quota enforcement.
Add disk-chaos QEMU tests that write, reboot, interrupt, corrupt one slot, compact, and prove deterministic recovery.
Gate storage on benchmark thresholds for write, read, replay, compaction, and memory pressure at target data sizes.
next_actions: Add a focused storage durability QEMU target that reuses the native store image across forced reboots.

tracks.title: Boot, attestation, and base update trust chain
current_evidence: Freestanding boot records can be verified against signed artifact manifests and compared across native smoke boots.
Remote attestation refuses emulator-rooted measured state and requires a provisioned non-software root.
A/B base selection, rollback, and post-activation health markers are covered by host and QEMU smoke evidence.

The native smoke target now includes negative QEMU runs that reject a tampered boot artifact manifest, direct kernel/userspace-image/policy/driver-set measurement tampering, and a rollback target whose slot measurement no longer verifies before the boot can reach native-ready.
The signature envelope and signing CLI now support both Ed25519 and an Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 hybrid preview profile with fail-closed verification for unsupported formats.

A signature-provider boundary and registry now report provider profile, release eligibility, and fail-closed profile mismatches so production Ed25519, ML-DSA, or hybrid providers can be swapped in without changing manifest storage layouts.

Userspace package signatures, boot artifact manifest signatures, generated archive signatures, and attestation statement signatures now route through the default provider registry instead of directly selecting raw Ed25519 operations.

Demo seed packages, SDK simulator release bundles, rendered-shell journeys, package-service fixtures, and spec release fixtures now select the Ed25519 provider explicitly where they model release signing behavior.
production_gaps: Host evidence still uses emulator-provided measurement fallbacks, and attestation root material is represented by software signer identities.
There is no hardware-backed provisioning, rotation, revocation, or verifier protocol boundary for TPM or secure-enclave roots.
The Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 hybrid profile is a bounded preview commitment for envelope and policy plumbing, not a FIPS 204 ML-DSA implementation.
Release artifact signing and bootloader measurement handoff now have smoke-level tamper rejection, but are not yet tied to an operational key-management story.
graduation_criteria: Introduce a hardware-root abstraction that supports TPM and secure enclave backed quote/sign operations without exposing root seed material.
Add verifier-facing attestation request and response records with nonce, remote party, policy visibility, key rotation, and revocation tests.
Replace the hybrid preview commitment with an audited FIPS 204 ML-DSA provider or an explicitly documented production cryptographic provider boundary.
Broaden release-image tamper gates from smoke fixtures to direct bootloader measurement mutation cases under operational signing keys.
next_actions: Split software signer provisioning out of attestation_service into a test-only provider.
Add a production root provider interface and a fake TPM provider used only by adversarial tests.
Move explicit software-provider release fixtures onto operational key provisioning once the hardware-backed root and release key-management interfaces exist.
Add a direct bootloader-measurement mutation fixture and bind the smoke signing path to the production root-provider abstraction.

tracks.title: First real hardware target: Intel NUC11TNKi5
current_evidence: The first supported hardware target is pinned to Intel NUC 11 Pro Kit NUC11TNKi5 instead of a generic PC-compatible bucket.

The target contract enumerates UEFI boot, ACPI tables, APIC timer, GOP framebuffer, USB xHCI input, NVMe block I/O, Intel I225-LM network, suspend/resume, and crash recovery as required hardware markers.
The build exposes an OVMF-backed uefi-qemu-test preflight for the ISO path before attempting the same image on the NUC firmware.
The kernel tree now has a tested ACPI RSDP parser and aligned scanner as the first non-invasive ACPI building block for the target.
The kernel tree now has a tested MADT parser that summarizes local APIC, I/O APIC, interrupt-source override, x2APIC, and PC-AT compatibility data before APIC timer bring-up.
The kernel tree now has a tested FADT parser for PM control blocks, SCI interrupt, PM timer, and reset register plumbing needed before suspend/resume work.
The kernel tree now has a tested UEFI GOP-style linear framebuffer descriptor validator with stride, buffer-size, pixel-format, and text-grid checks.
The kernel tree now has a bounded crash-record format with checksum validation and redacted summary output for later persistent crash recovery.
PCI inventory helpers now identify NVMe controllers and the Intel I225-LM network controller required by the NUC target.
The kernel tree now has a tested NVMe inventory shim with controller-capability parsing, admin-queue validation, and fail-closed data-plane transfer behavior.
The kernel tree now has a tested Intel I225-LM inventory shim with RX/TX ring-plan validation and fail-closed kernel transmit behavior.
The kernel tree now has a tested xHCI input inventory shim with controller-capability parsing, command/event ring validation, and fail-closed USB input report behavior.

Production readiness rejects QEMU-only evidence for this target; hardware proof requires captured real-machine logs, firmware settings, power-cycle notes, and repeated cold boot, reboot, suspend/resume, storage, network, and crash-recovery cycles.
production_gaps: The repo does not yet emit the NUC11TNKi5 hardware markers from a real boot.
UEFI handoff still depends on the GRUB ISO path and has not been proven on the selected NUC firmware.
The ACPI RSDP parser is tested but not wired to a UEFI or BIOS memory-map handoff during boot.
The MADT parser is tested but not wired to local APIC, I/O APIC, or APIC timer programming during boot.
The FADT parser is tested but not wired to ACPI sleep-state discovery, wake, or reset execution.
The framebuffer descriptor validator is tested but not wired to the bootloader's GOP framebuffer handoff during boot.
Crash record formatting is tested but not persisted before reboot or consumed by recovery boot.
PCI target identification, NVMe controller queue validation, and Intel I225-LM ring planning are tested, but NVMe read/write and Intel I225-LM packet I/O drivers are not implemented.
xHCI capability parsing and ring validation are tested, but USB HID keyboard enumeration and input reports are not implemented.
Suspend/resume and crash recovery need real-device implementations and logs.
graduation_criteria: Boot the NUC11TNKi5 from a UEFI USB image built from the repo and archive the serial/framebuffer proof bundle.
Emit and verify every marker in spec/hardware/nuc11tnki5-required-markers.txt from real hardware.
Pass the minimum cycle counts encoded by hardware_target.first_supported_target without panic, hang, unredacted crash data, or persistence loss.
Keep QEMU smoke, storage durability, driver restart, recovery, and spec gates green before accepting hardware proof as production evidence.
next_actions: Make build/os.iso boot reliably through the NUC11TNKi5 UEFI firmware and record firmware settings.
Add ACPI table discovery and APIC timer proof markers before replacing PIT/PIC assumptions on the target.
Add GOP framebuffer, xHCI keyboard, NVMe, and Intel I225-LM userspace-driver proof markers.
Add suspend/resume and induced crash-recovery loops to the NUC proof runbook.

tracks.title: Userspace launch and service image provenance
current_evidence: The build generates a userspace image archive and production artifact manifest for freestanding boot profiles.
Launch provenance, component ABI metadata, signed bundle state, and syscall-dispatched task creation are enforced in native modules.
Negative tests reject unsigned userspace launches and modeled runtime bypasses.
The production-readiness gate rejects unmarked syntheticUserspaceImage fixtures in critical launch and service test paths; existing synthetic fixtures are marked model-only.
production_gaps: Many host tests still rely on syntheticUserspaceImage records instead of built image descriptors.
The production archive path needs negative tests for missing image bytes, mismatched digest, bad ELF metadata, and stale generated manifests.
Service launch health and restart behavior need stronger evidence across real userspace image startup rather than in-process model state.
graduation_criteria: Replace critical launch-path synthetic image tests with fixtures derived from generated userspace image artifacts.
Add stale, truncated, unsigned, and digest-mismatched userspace archive tests to the spec gate.
Add a QEMU service-startup proof that exercises mailbox, descriptor validation, syscall query, heartbeat, fault, and restart paths from real images.
next_actions: Create a small generated-image fixture reader for host tests.
Replace the marked model-only launch and service synthetic fixtures with generated userspace image fixtures.
Extend userspace archive generation tests around production_artifact_manifest.zig.

tracks.title: Live sync and private overlay transport
current_evidence: Sync state covers device graph enrollment, selective policy, CRDT merge semantics, secret transfer markers, transactional database contracts, and conflict recording.
The overlay relay service rejects unauthorized relay use and target changes in harnessed tests.
End-to-end host tests replicate document, media, secret, and database payloads between two service tasks through a booted relay fallback model.
production_gaps: Transport is still an in-process harness with bounded packet queues and no async network driver, reconnect, replay-window, or congestion story.
Multi-device evidence does not yet run as separate QEMU nodes with real network packets and independently persisted stores.
Device identity depends on the boot/attestation production root track before remote trust can be considered production-grade.
graduation_criteria: Replace sync_transport_harness as the primary evidence with a native transport service that runs through endpoint syscalls and the network driver task.
Add two-node QEMU replication tests covering offline edits, reconnect, relay fallback, replay rejection, duplicate frame handling, and persisted restart.
Bind remote device sessions to production attestation roots or explicitly mark them local-lab only.
next_actions: Define the transport service ABI and move packet submission out of the harness module.
Add durable outbound and inbound frame queues to sync_state_store.
Create a two-QEMU sync smoke harness with separate native-store images.

tracks.title: Userspace driver data-plane depth
current_evidence: Driver registration checks signed bundles, device-class authority, DMA range metadata, restart generations, and a constrained first target of brokered programmed-I/O ATA rather than bus-master DMA.
Storage driver tasks attach through the kernel device broker and the ATA bootstrap path exports checked read/write bridges for freestanding volume access.

The driver boundary spec gate exercises brokered ATA read/write I/O and rejects stale task authority, stale broker sessions, expired leases, invalid ports, explicit broker revocation, and post-restart target generation mismatches.

The storage data-plane gate covers timeout propagation, active-I/O restart, and partial-transfer recovery by proving incomplete ATA writes are discarded before a restarted userspace driver reissues I/O.

The native network driver path reauthorizes brokered service-identity sends through the egress broker, so revoked network-policy capabilities stop already-open userspace network paths before transmit.

QEMU driver restart proof performs broker-mediated storage reads and writes before and after restart, rejects stale authority and stale DMA/port access after generation change, and gates the new broker session rebind.
production_gaps: Only the bootstrap storage path has concrete hardware-like data-plane depth; other driver classes remain inventory, policy, or publication proofs.
IOMMU and DMA isolation are represented as native policy records and a constrained programmed-I/O first target rather than hardware programming and fault evidence.
The timeout, partial-transfer, and explicit revocation cases are host spec gates; QEMU coverage still centers on brokered restart and rebind.
graduation_criteria: Add broker-mediated data-plane tests for at least storage and network that run in QEMU and prove no kernel direct publication for excluded subsystems.
Add DMA/IOMMU programming interfaces before broadening the first production target beyond brokered programmed-I/O storage.
Gate driver restart on active I/O recovery, broker revocation, rebind, and no stale DMA or port access after generation change.
next_actions: Move timeout, partial transfer, and explicit broker revocation proofs into the focused QEMU driver restart gate.
Define the hardware IOMMU programming interface required before enabling bus-master DMA targets.

tracks.title: Resource scheduler and live platform telemetry
current_evidence: Scheduler decisions account for resource class, engine availability, thermal pressure, battery saver, privacy mode, CPU budget, memory bandwidth, and zero-copy shared memory.
Booted provider tests derive hardware-source telemetry from live runtime counters instead of purely synthetic state.
Telemetry now flows through an explicit provider boundary with test-only host fakes and production freestanding provider descriptors.
Negative tests require observed telemetry before waking hardware queues.
production_gaps: The freestanding provider is still assembled from native runtime counters and test-provided platform fields, not real ACPI, battery, thermal, GPU, NPU, or media driver sources.
There is no scheduler latency, fairness, starvation, or thermal regression gate under sustained load.
Accelerator availability is represented by booleans rather than device queue ownership and completion interrupts.
graduation_criteria: Introduce platform telemetry providers for the first supported target and mark emulator-only providers as test-only.
Add benchmark gates for scheduler latency, fairness across resource classes, background throttling, and thermal/battery policy transitions.
Tie accelerator claims to brokered device queues or explicitly limit production support to CPU/media classes.
next_actions: Replace the freestanding runtime-counter bridge with first-target ACPI, battery, thermal, GPU, NPU, and media driver readers.
Add scheduler benchmark fixtures that run under the existing QEMU benchmark target.
Add regression tests for starvation and privacy-sensitive workload throttling.
